doc.title: Bill Holman interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 13, 1999

title: Keeping scores and tracking down Barnet charts
summary: He kept copies only after 1970 and is trying to recover Barnet charts from the estate.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Do you have a basement full of scores?
Yes. I have a whole house full. Scores and CDs are going to run me out of my house.
I’m wondering if you’ve been able to keep the original scores of most of the work you’ve done.

Up until about 1970, very few of them because before then they weren’t able to Xerox the oversized sheets, so you’d write a chart and you’d just give it to the band leader and that’s the last you’d see. Now I make a Xerox of everything before I give it to the employer, whoever it was, so I have most everything. I’ve got some of the older things, the things that I recorded myself. I’m trying to find some of the things that I wrote for Charlie Barnet for those two albums we did. I’m trying to locate those with the thought of maybe getting published. So I talked to a guy who knows a guy who knows where they are and he sent me a list and there’s quite a few of the scores in there that I hadn’t seen for 30 years.

Well I guess Barnet’s estate, but they gave part of them to a school and they gave — I think some of the others were just in Charlie’s house and they gave them to this guy to go back, and he lives in Philadelphia, and he’s going to get them in shape again and he’s going to put them in a collection somewhere.
